A 38-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by ambulance with altered mental
status. She is comatose but exhibits spontaneous deep and rapid breathing. Her vital signs are:
temperature 100.1°F, blood pressure 101/58 mmHg, heart rate 103 bpm, respiratory rate 24, and
oxygen saturation 97% on room air. Laboratory results include: WBC 12,700/µL, hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL,
platelets 254,000/µL, sodium 137 mEq/L, potassium 4.2 mEq/L, chloride 100 mEq/L, bicarbonate 16
mEq/L, and creatinine 1.78 mg/dL. Arterial blood gas reveals pH 7.38, PaO2 94 mmHg, and PaCO2 26
mmHg. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s condition? Answer Choices: (A) Salicylate toxicity
(B) Medication overdose (C) Acute kidney injury with uremia (D) Alcohol binging (E) Undiagnosed type
1 diabetes mellitus (F) Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (G) Lactic acidosis due to hypoperfusion (H)
Starvation-induced ketoacidosis (I) Early septic shock with metabolic compensation (J) Severe sepsis
 A. Early septic shock with metabolic compensation
B. Medication overdose
C. Starvation-induced ketoacidosis
D. Undiagnosed type 1 diabetes mellitus
E. Acute kidney injury with uremia
F. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
G. Lactic acidosis due to hypoperfusion
